text:
Bolt Action - Official Gameplay Trailer
Take a look at gameplay from Bolt Action in this latest trailer for the upcoming turn-based World War 2 strategy inspired by Warlord Games’ tabletop classic. In Bolt Action, step into the boots of a battlefield commander. The new trailer gives a peek at gameplay, including the game's dynamic activation system, tactical Orders, indirect fire, flanking maneuvers, and the strategic decision-making that defines every battle. Bolt Action will be available on PC (Steam, GOG, and Epic Games Store).

See how the Bolt Action game adapts the iconic Order Dice mechanic for digital play. This gameplay footage demonstrates how dynamic activations create a reactive battlefield experience.

This video showcases an in-development build of the digital adaptation, focusing on how the Order Dice mechanic changes traditional turn structures. By replacing static turns with unpredictable activations, the game forces players to adapt their wargaming strategy on the fly. If you enjoy turn-based tactics or tabletop wargames, this look at the digital interface provides a clear picture of how the rules translate from the tabletop to the screen.

We examine the core flow of combat in Bolt Action digital, specifically highlighting how the reactive nature of the Order Dice mechanic impacts decision-making. Whether you are a long-time fan of the physical game or new to the system, this footage explains the fundamental shift in tactical pacing you can expect when commanding your units.

Wishlist the game to stay updated on development progress and subscribe for more strategy game gameplay breakdowns.

text:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day Review
Tom Holland is back for a fourth solo outing as Spider-Man in Brand New Day. Along with Brand New director, Destin Daniel Cretton, your friendly neighborhood webslinger is up against a mysterious new antagonist (cast just as mysteriously with Sadie Sink), but where the title might hint at a fresh start for Peter Parker, can the film itself go back to basics and deliver everything you need from a Spider-Man story? IGN's Tom Jorgensen reviews the movie to talk about that, how Punisher is a great uncle and why only one actor is a little bit wasted.
